## [6.2.0](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/compare/code-review-action@v6.1.0...code-review-action@v6.2.0) (2026-08-13)

## Release Notes

The two improvements in this release tighten how the action gathers codebase context — ensuring it actually uses the source it selected and gets smarter results from Graphify before giving up on it.

## ✨ What's New

### Graphify Queries Now Refine Before Falling Back

When Autopilot's Graphify tier returns a truncated or empty graph answer, it now narrows the query and tries again before falling back to ordinary file search. Previously, the first answer was treated as complete even when it was clearly incomplete. Now, Graphify ends each context pass with a bounded shortlist and writes a `graphify-trace:` line recording query count, truncation events, shortlist size, and any reads outside the shortlist. The shortlist is also carried forward in the Context Map's Snapshot section so later phases (review, react) reuse what the graph already found rather than re-querying.

In practice, this means context gathered during a review run will be more complete and consistent — reducing cases where the AI misses relevant files because an initial Graphify response was cut short.

<details><summary>Related issues</summary>

- [#587: Make Graphify context gathering refine broad or truncated queries](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/issues/587)
- [#589: Refine Graphify queries before falling back to file search](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/pull/589)
</details>

### Linear Runs Now Prove They Used the Context Source They Selected

Linear-run jobs (both stored-plan and fresh-plan) now fail the context phase with a clear error if codebase context was gathered without recording which source — Graphify or Repomix — was actually used. Previously, a run could silently fall back to ordinary file search even when a specific context source had been selected, making it impossible to know what the AI was working from. That silent fallback is now blocked.

If you operate Linear-integrated workflows, any run that previously succeeded by quietly skipping context source verification will now surface as a context-phase failure instead. This is intentional — it's better to know the run didn't meet its configured constraints than to get a review based on incomplete or unverified context.

<details><summary>Related issues</summary>

- [#586: Make linear-run enforce Graphify or Repomix context selection](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/issues/586)
- [#588: Make Linear runs prove they used the codebase source they selected](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/pull/588)
</details>
